Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS)

AGITATION AND SEDATION ASSESSMENT

Measures the level of agitation or sedation in critically ill patients, aiding in the titration of medications in the ICU.
Patient Data

Fill out for the Medical Record/PDF Report

Clinical Criteria
Select the clinical level that describes the patient.

Final RASS Score

Assessment Memory

Suggested NANDA Diagnoses
Based on the agitation or sedation level of the critically ill patient.

Processing clinical reasoning...

Frequently Asked Questions
Follow more nursing information on our Nursing Forum.

Related Scales
Ramsay Scale Assessment of sedation level.

Glasgow Scale Assessment of consciousness level.

FOUR Scale Advanced neurological assessment in the ICU.

Scientific Reference
SESSLER, C. N. et al. The Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS): Validity and reliability in adult intensive care unit patients. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. , v. 166, p. 1338-44, 2002.

Score Interpretation

Agitation (+1 to +4)
Agitated or aggressive patient. Requires intervention for patient and staff safety.

Alert and Calm (0)
Ideal sedation goal for most patients (awake and cooperative).

Light/Moderate Sedation (-1 to -3)
The patient responds to verbal stimuli, indicating a controlled sedation plan.

Deep Sedation / Coma (-4 to -5)
No response to verbal stimuli. Responds only to rigorous physical stimulus or is unresponsive.
